newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index down 0.1 pct at 313.67.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index down 0.1 pct at 313.67.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, fell 0.1 percent to 313.67 at the start of play on Monday.
Latin America edged down 1.3 percent day-on-day to 579.25, Asia was flat at 262.13, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 1.7 percent at 147.88.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high this year of 314.10 after the close of play on January 20.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was down 0.38 percent day-on-day at 169.97 at 1000 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high of 171.22 after the end of trading on January 20.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was up 0.27 percent at 508.210, calculated after the close of trade on Thursday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. Its 1997 high of 508.674 was also reached on January 20.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, fell 0.8 percent to 125.86 by the start of trade on Monday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996, and reached a 1997 high of 125.93 after the close of trade on 16 January.
By region, Latin America was down 0.26 percent at 104.47, Asia fell 0.01 to 132.43 and East Europe was down 0.17 at 160.61. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
